note: Each country's policy numbers set against at least one source independent of the one used. Verdicts: match (within rounding), consistent (agrees once scope is aligned), corrected (our number changed after the check), differs (scope differs; explained), single source.

rows.item: Budget 2025 scorecard, sum of the 88 measures vs HMT's total row (£m, 2025-26 to 2030-31)
rows.verdict: match

rows.item: Largest Budget 2025 measures, 2029-30 (£bn): threshold freeze; salary sacrifice; two-child limit; EV mileage duty; gambling
rows.source: OBR, Economic and fiscal outlook, November 2025
rows.verdict: match

rows.item: IT+NIC fiscal-drag elasticities: frozen-threshold ε; CPI-indexed ε; £bn per +1pp earnings under the freeze (2025-26 IT+NIC base)
rows.other: para 4.14: +£7bn under freeze vs ~£4.5bn if CPI-indexed; RR Mar 2025 Earnings level → PAYE+NICs same-year £6.1bn (2025-26) to £7.4bn (2029-30)
rows.source: OBR EFO October 2026 para 4.14; OBR ready reckoner March 2025
rows.verdict: consistent: ε=1.3 and 1.3×4.5/7 from the paragraph; RR £m coefficients match the £7bn order. Budget 2025 Personal Tax (threshold extension to April 2031) stays in the policy line only

rows.item: Budget 2025 total effect on borrowing, 2029-30 (£bn)
rows.verdict: differs: OBR also counts decisions outside the Budget, chiefly the July 2025 welfare U-turn (+6.9), which reversed cuts our model never assumed

rows.item: Budget 2026 total effect on borrowing (£bn, 2026-27 to 2031-32)
rows.verdict: differs: OBR's total includes indirect effects and debt interest, which our static line leaves out by design; the scorecard reconciles exactly to HMT's Table 6.1
